_doc: Voice & concept spec for the NFRI whitepaper essays. INTERNAL harness config — not rendered to the site. Encodes the target register (incisive market-essay + academic rigour) and the conceptual frames the model justification should deploy, so rewrites are held to a consistent standard. harness/style_check.py lints the essay contracts against this. No external author/firm names appear here by policy; the register is described abstractly.
voice_rules: Open each movement with a load-bearing claim or a concrete locus, not background or throat-clearing.
Open in scene when earned — curtailment notice, queue screen, bind moment — before abstract thesis.
Organise the field with an explicit taxonomy before analysing it (kinds of model, layers, reasons).
Put a real company, a real number, or a dated fact in the same sentence as each claim.
State economics as a named mechanism or a back-of-envelope rule of thumb (load × hours × penalty).
Alternate short declarative thesis sentences with one longer sentence that carries the machinery.
Use first person/plural only when marking a field locus or the limit of a claim — never to decorate.
Name civilizational stakes once per act — reindustrialisation requires honest cover, not damage-default renewal.
Call out discourse laundering when availability loss is treated as settled under damage wordings.
Borrow one outside frame as a lens (compound loss, correlation substrate, indicator) and test the case against it.
Fire-take pulls between beats: one italic sentence, load-bearing, no hedge.
Name the strongest objection explicitly, then answer it.
Close on a turn or a reframe the reader could not have started with — who carries unrated availability — never a summary.
Gloss field jargon inline the first time (MGA, binder, non-firm, curtailment, expectile).

anti_patterns.why: even-handed hedging instead of a position
anti_patterns.regex: (?i)\b(pros and cons|on the one hand|there are (both )?(advantages|benefits) and|it depends)

anti_patterns.why: stacked adjectives doing a fact's job
abstract noun with no concrete referent

anti_patterns.regex: (?i)\b(at the end of the day|going forward|key takeaway|deep dive into the|unlock(ing)? value)

concept_frames.deploy: Name the dated, exogenous shift that made the exposure newly insurable (always-on compute; connections reform).
Frame the cover as a product that does not yet exist, not a better version of an existing one.
Never sell the index without naming its basis risk: triggers buy speed/cost at the price of payout-loss mismatch.
Justify why a risk-averse buyer takes imperfect cover, and where demand goes to zero.
Present the payout function as a designed object (conditional expectile of true loss), not a lookup.
Define the index as a Critical Risk Indicator: an observable proxy for an unobservable system risk.
State the real-world variable the risk correlates through (grid geography), and that basis risk is the residual.
Treat curtailment as frequency × severity, both moving with constraints not condition.
Justify the latent×deterministic blend as credibility weighting, not an average of opinions.
Make the implicit thesis explicit: an observable, rising cost meets a flat rate — the definition of mispricing.
Name the narrow wedge and the platform it expands into; the measurement is the moat, not underwriting cleverness.
Show where damage BI stands in for availability cover — contested loss type treated as renewal default.
Name what the build requires (firm electrons, register honesty) and what breaks if curtailment stays unpriced.
Hold grid capacity, market structure, and builder economics in the same frame — three lenses on one interruptible-connection bet.

terminology._doc: Site prose: do not use 'peril' as generic shorthand for non-firm availability. Reserve peril for LMA 'insured peril', cat 'named perils', or 'physical perils'. Prefer availability risk, curtailment exposure, loss mechanism, time-element loss.
